newsitem.title: USA: Carrington Lab oral products label expanded.
newsitem.headline: Carrington Lab oral products label expanded.

text.p: Carrington Laboratories Inc said on Thursday it received clearance from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration to add new label indications to two of products for treatment of oral mucositis or stomatitis.

The label indications applied the company's Radiacare oral wound rinse, formulated for mucositis, and its Carrington Patch, a patch placed inside the mouth to manage canker sores and other types of mouth sores, Carrington said.
Oral mucositis/stomatitis is a painful inflammation of the oral mucosa, often involving the palate, tongue, gums, cheek or other areas of the oral cavity, the company said.
It was common among patients undergoing chemotherapy or radiation for head and neck cancer.

"The current clearance to market expands the potential market for the RadiaCare line to include the management of conditions other than radiation-induced dermatitis," the company said. "Certainly these are attractive markets with existing unmet needs. We will market these products through our existing sales force and will be seeking co- marketers."

The company also said its new RadiaCare line would consist of six products -- the oral wound rinse, cleansing agent RadiaCare Klenz, RadiaCare Gel and Gel Sheet to manage dermatitis induced by radiation, moisturizing RadiaCare Cream, and RadiaCare Sun Block & Lip Balm.
